_meta.indication: Treatment of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in adult patients who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody positive

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 309JG (BN40900), also referred to as Study 1 in the label
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating satralizumab as monotherapy (without concurrent immunosuppressive therapy)
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with NMOSD; 64 were anti-AQP4 antibody positive and 31 were anti-AQP4 antibody negative
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to the first Clinical Endpoint Committee (CEC)-confirmed relapse (protocol-defined relapse)
pivotal_trials.n: 95 patients randomized (satralizumab n=63, placebo n=32); 64 anti-AQP4 positive (41 satralizumab, 23 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: In the anti-AQP4 antibody positive population, 74% risk reduction in time to first relapse (hazard ratio 0.26; 95% CI 0.11, 0.63; p=0.0014); relapse in 9 (22%) of ENSPRYNG vs 13 (56.5%) placebo. No benefit in anti-AQP4 negative patients.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 307JG (BN40898), also referred to as Study 2 in the label
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating satralizumab as add-on to a stable dose of baseline immunosuppressant therapy (IST)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with NMOSD on stable baseline IST; included seven pediatric patients (ages 12-17) and 76 adult patients; in the ITT population 52 were anti-AQP4 positive and 31 were anti-AQP4 negative
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to the first Clinical Endpoint Committee (CEC)-confirmed relapse (protocol-defined relapse)
pivotal_trials.n: 83 patients randomized (satralizumab n=41, placebo n=42); 52 anti-AQP4 positive (26 satralizumab, 26 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: In the anti-AQP4 antibody positive population, 78% risk reduction in time to first relapse (hazard ratio 0.22; 95% CI 0.06, 0.82; p=0.0143); relapse in 3 (11.5%) of ENSPRYNG+IST vs 11 (42.3%) placebo+IST. No benefit in anti-AQP4 negative patients.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence at least 15%): nasopharyngitis, headache, upper respiratory tract infection, gastritis, rash, arthralgia, extremity pain, fatigue, and nausea. In Study 2 nasopharyngitis (31% vs 15% placebo) and headache (27% vs 12%). Key warnings: infections (including serious infections), elevated liver enzymes, and decreased neutrophil counts.
target_moa: Humanized IgG2 monoclonal antibody that binds the interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor, preventing IL-6 binding and inhibiting IL-6 signaling through soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptor

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile is similar to other biologics with similar mechanisms, the trial designs were acceptable, and the efficacy findings were clear.

summary.text: The satralizumab-mwge development program for NMOSD was granted fast track designation (October 31, 2013), orphan drug designation (June 30, 2014), and breakthrough therapy designation (December 18, 2018). The BLA was received August 15, 2019 and approved August 14, 2020 under a standard (non-accelerated) approval based on two adequate and well-controlled trials; because of the orphan designation the sponsor was exempt from PREA pediatric assessment requirements.

requirement.text: PMR 3920-1: A worldwide single-arm pregnancy safety study to collect and analyze information for a minimum of 10 years on pregnancy complications and birth outcomes in women exposed to Enspryng during pregnancy in patients with NMOSD.

citations.quote: 3920-1 A worldwide single-arm pregnancy safety study to collect and analyze information for a minimum of 10 years on pregnancy complications and birth outcomes in women exposed to Enspryng (satrializumab-mwge) during pregnancy in patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD). Provide a complete protocol that includes details regarding how you plan to encourage patients and providers to report pregnancy exposures, measures to ensure complete data capture regarding pregnancy outcomes and any adverse effects in offspring, and plans for comprehensive data analysis.
